idiom-31-q16.truthCondition: Ava and Ruby have angry arguments whenever they are near each other.
idiom-31-q16.correctReason: 原題說艾娃和露比每次靠近便激烈爭吵；正確句保留「whenever」的反覆觸發關係。

foils.text: Ava and Ruby fight like cat and dog only when they are far apart.
foils.reason: 「far apart」把觸發情況由靠近對方改成遠離對方。

foils.text: Ava and Ruby fought like cat and dog once when they sat together.
foils.reason: 「once」把每次靠近都會吵的模式改成單次事件。

foils.text: Ava and Ruby avoid angry arguments whenever they are near each other.
foils.reason: 「avoid」說兩人靠近時能避免爭吵，與原題相反。

idiom-31-q17.truthCondition: Daniel and his younger sister love each other but argue fiercely over tiny matters.
idiom-31-q17.correctReason: 正確句同時保留兩人彼此關愛、卻會為小事激烈爭吵的對比；爭吵不等於彼此憎恨。

foils.text: Daniel and his younger sister fight like cat and dog over small things because they hate each other.
foils.reason: 「hate each other」與原題說兩人彼此關愛直接衝突。

foils.text: Daniel and his younger sister fight like cat and dog only over major problems, despite loving each other.
foils.reason: 「only over major problems」把爭議由小事改成重大問題。

foils.text: Daniel and his younger sister love each other and never argue fiercely over small things.
foils.reason: 「never argue」否定了原題所說的激烈爭吵。

idiom-31-q18.truthCondition: The brothers were already in another fierce argument when their father arrived home.
idiom-31-q18.correctReason: 「were fighting」表示父親回到家時，兩兄弟正吵得激烈；「again」保留又一次爭吵。

foils.text: The brothers started fighting like cat and dog only after their father came home.
foils.reason: 「only after」把爭吵開始時間移到父親到家後；原題說父親到家時爭吵已在進行。

foils.text: The brothers stopped fighting like cat and dog when their father came home.
foils.reason: 「stopped」說父親到家時爭吵已停止；原題說當時仍在吵。

foils.text: The brothers were fighting like cat and dog for the first time when their father came home.
foils.reason: 「for the first time」與原題的「another」相反。

idiom-31-q19.truthCondition: Kate reports that her two cousins always argue angrily while planning a holiday.
idiom-31-q19.correctReason: 正確句保留凱特的轉述、兩名表親，以及每次計劃旅行都會激烈爭吵的習慣。

foils.text: Kate says her two cousins fight like cat and dog whenever they return from a holiday.
foils.reason: 「return from」把爭吵時點由計劃旅行改成旅行回來之後。

foils.text: Kate says her two cousins sometimes fight like cat and dog when planning a holiday.
foils.reason: 「sometimes」弱化原題的「always」，不再是每次計劃都吵。

foils.text: Kate says her two cousins calmly agree whenever they plan a holiday.
foils.reason: 「calmly agree」把激烈爭吵改成平靜達成共識。

idiom-31-q20.truthCondition: The speaker and his brother argued angrily throughout childhood but are close now.
idiom-31-q20.correctText: My brother and I fought like cat and dog all the time as children, but we are close now.
idiom-31-q20.correctZh: 我和哥哥小時候總是激烈爭吵，但現在關係親密。
idiom-31-q20.answerOverrideReason: Restores the source's explicit all-the-time childhood frequency and present closeness; the canonical source answer remains unchanged.
idiom-31-q20.correctReason: 「all the time as children」保留童年總是爭吵的頻率；「but we are close now」保留如今關係親密的轉變。

foils.text: My brother and I still fight like cat and dog, although we were close as children.
foils.reason: 這句把時間線倒轉：原題說童年常吵、如今親密。

foils.text: My brother and I used to fight like cat and dog as children, and we still do now.
foils.reason: 「we still do now」說現在仍常吵，與原題現時關係親密的轉變不符。

foils.text: My brother and I hardly ever fought as children, but we are close now.
foils.reason: 「hardly ever fought」把童年總是激烈爭吵改成很少爭吵。
